diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $R>0$ such that $\Omega_\epsilon\subset B_R(0)$,  and consider   a window $g\in\mathcal{C}_c^\infty(\rr d)$ such that $g=1$

issues.failure_explanation: The key step $\hat h(\xi)=V_g h(x,\xi)$ on $\Omega_\epsilon$ uses a window $g$ with $g=1$ on $B_{2R}(0)$, $R$ depending on $\Omega$; the resulting inequality is then treated as a statement about the fixed-window modulation norm with an $\Omega$-independent constant $C_{d,n}$ (and with constant exactly 1 in the lemmas). The window-change constants depend on $\Omega$ and are not tracked. Scaling shows the claim is false: for $\Omega=B_R$, the right-hand side behaves like $R^{d(1-1/s-1/p)}$ (or $R^{d(1-d/s-1/p)}$ with the stated exponent $-d/p$), which tends to 0 as $R\to\infty$ when $1/s+1/p>1$ (e.g. $p\le1$), while the left-hand side tends to $\|f\|_{W^{n,r}(\rr d)}>0$. The same hidden window dependence affects lem:added-1 (constant $|\Omega|^{-1/p}$), the converse lemma and its convex corollary (constant $|\Omega+\Omega|^{1/p}$ with a window whose support is inside $\Omega$ and a translation step justified only up to $\asymp$). Also the proof derives $|\Omega_\epsilon|^{-1/p}$ but the statements carry $|\Omega|^{-d/p}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate all these results with constants depending on $\Omega$ (through the window change), or fix a reference window and track the equivalence constants explicitly; replace $|\Omega|^{-d/p}$ by the derived $|\Omega|^{-1/p}$.
issues.overall_effect: All explicit $\Omega$-dependence of the constants in Section 3 (and the factors $|\Omega+\Omega|$, $2|\Omega|$ advertised in prop:supported and cor:Barron) is unsupported and in part false; only qualitative embeddings with $\Omega$-dependent constants survive.
issues.title: Local M^{p,q}–FL^q comparisons hide an Omega-dependent window; explicit constants are false as stated
issues.why_classification: The qualitative embeddings remain true but the advertised explicit constants must be withdrawn or re-derived with a nontrivial tracking of window-dependence; several stated inequalities are false as written.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated for all $0<q\le\infty$, but the proof bounds $\|F*\check g\|_{L^q}$ by $\|F\|_{L^q}\|\check g\|_{L^1}$, which is Young's inequality and is false on $L^q$ for $q<1$ (also the weight $v_s$ is dropped from the $L^1$ norm of $\check g$). For $q<1$ a different argument (e.g. Plancherel–Polya/Nikolskii type inequalities for Fourier transforms of compactly supported functions) is needed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the lemma to $1\le q\le\infty$, or supply the standard quasi-Banach argument for compactly supported functions (with a constant depending on $\Omega$ and $g$).
issues.overall_effect: The lemma (and hence prop:supported for $q<1$) is unproved in the quasi-Banach range $0<q<1$.
issues.title: Young's inequality step in the FL^q → M^{p,q} lemma fails for q<1
issues.why_classification: A standard local argument or a restriction of the range repairs it without affecting the main theorems.

issues.failure_explanation: For convex $\Omega$ one has $\Omega+\Omega=2\Omega$, whose Lebesgue measure is $2^d|\Omega|$. The proof's observation $|x+y|=2|z|$ concerns Euclidean norms, not measures, so the argument yields $|\Omega+\Omega|^{1/p}=2^{d/p}|\Omega|^{1/p}$, not the claimed $2^{1/p}|\Omega|^{1/p}$ when $d\ge2$.

failure_location.quote: Then the estimate~\eqref{stima1} can be improved by replacing \(|\Omega + \Omega|^{1/p}\) with \(2^{1/p} |\Omega|^{1/p}\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $2^{1/p}$ by $2^{d/p}$ (or absorb into the generic constant).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed constant in the convex case (and the factor '2C' in prop:supported and cor:Barron) is not established for $d\ge2$.
issues.title: Convex-domain improvement confuses norm scaling with measure: |Ω+Ω| = 2^d|Ω|, not 2|Ω|
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of a constant with no effect on rates or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, by selecting $r\geq 2$ and  $n\in \zzp{}$, it follows that $W^{n,r}(\Omega)$ is a type-2 Banach space

issues.failure_explanation: The statement allows any $r\ge2$, including $r=\infty$, but the proof invokes Maurey's bound (prop:approximation_type2), which requires a type-2 Banach space; $W^{n,\infty}(\Omega)\supset L^\infty(\Omega)$ is not of type 2, and the $N^{-1/2}$ convex-hull rate fails in $L^\infty$ in general. The same endpoint appears in the corollaries and in thm:approximation_sobolev_space_G.
issues.overall_effect: The endpoint $r=\infty$ is unsupported in all approximation theorems.
issues.title: Local theorem admits r=∞, but W^{n,∞}(Ω) is not type 2
issues.why_classification: Excluding a single unsupported endpoint preserves the method, rate and all substantive claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: M^2_{v_s}(\rr d) = L^2_s(\rr d)\cap \cF L^2_s(\rr d)= Q^s(\rr d)

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes $M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}\hookrightarrow M^1_{1\otimes v_{n+1}}$ for $s_1>d/2$, $s_2>n+1+d/2$, but then bounds the error by $\|f\|_{Q^{s_2}}$ or $\|f\|_{L^2_{s_1}}+\|f\|_{\mathscr FL^2_{s_2}}$. Neither norm dominates $\|f\|_{M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}}$: $Q^{s_2}=M^2_{\langle z\rangle^{s_2}}$ and $\langle x\rangle^{s_1}\langle\xi\rangle^{s_2}\not\lesssim\langle (x,\xi)\rangle^{s_2}$; and $L^2_{s_1}\cap\mathscr FL^2_{s_2}=M^2_{v_{s_1}\otimes1+1\otimes v_{s_2}}$ with $\langle x\rangle^{s_1}+\langle\xi\rangle^{s_2}\not\gtrsim\langle x\rangle^{s_1}\langle\xi\rangle^{s_2}$. Direct Cauchy–Schwarz shows $Q^{s}\hookrightarrow M^1_{1\otimes v_{n+1}}$ requires $s>n+1+d$, so the stated condition $s_2>n+1+d/2$ is insufficient for the first alternative, and the second alternative needs a different index condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the result for $\|f\|_{Q^{s}}$ with $s>n+1+d$ (equivalently $s=s_1+s_2$), and re-derive the correct index conditions for the $L^2_{s_1}\cap\mathscr FL^2_{s_2}$ variant.
issues.overall_effect: Both bounds in eq:Hilbert_approximation_bound_L are unsupported under the stated indices; the 'uncertainty principle' interpretation rests on them.
issues.title: Shubin–Sobolev corollary: Q^{s_2} and L^2_{s_1}∩FL^2_{s_2} norms do not dominate the tensor-weighted M^2 norm used
issues.why_classification: A comparable corollary survives, but with strictly stronger weight indices and a corrected embedding argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $f\in M^{p,q}_{1\otimes v_{s_2}}(\rr d)$, with $0<p<\infty$, $0<q\leq 2\leq r$,

issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side is $\|f\|_{\mathscr FL^q_{v_{s_2}}}$ for the unlocalized $f$, but Theorem local needs $\|f\|_{M^{p,q}_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}}$, and $\mathscr FL^q_{v_s}\not\hookrightarrow M^{p,q}_{1\otimes v_s}$ for $p<\infty$ (modulation spaces with $p<\infty$ encode spatial decay, Fourier–Lebesgue spaces do not). The invoked lemma concerns $\chi_\Omega f$, but approximating $\chi_\Omega f$ would require $\chi_\Omega f\in\mathscr FL^q_{v_{s_2}}$ with $s_2>n+1\ge1$, which fails for a hard cutoff (jump discontinuity gives only $|\xi|^{-1}$ decay). Moreover for $p>1$ the theorem requires $s_1>d/p'$, while the proposition assumes only the weight $1\otimes v_{s_2}$. cor:Barron ($p=q=1$) inherits the defect: $\|f\|_{M^1_{1\otimes v_{n+1}}}\not\lesssim\|f\|_{B_{n+1}}$.

failure_location.quote: The proof is a combination of \cref{thm:approximation_sobolev_space_local} and \cref{cor:FourierLebesgue_embedding_in_modulation_space} as well as \cref{cor:FourierLebesgue_embedding_in_modulation_space_convex}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Theorem local to $\psi f$ with a smooth cutoff $\psi\in C_c^\infty$, $\psi=1$ on $\Omega$, using $\|\psi f\|_{M^{p,q}_{1\otimes v_{s_2}}}\lesssim_{\psi}\|\psi f\|_{\mathscr FL^q_{v_{s_2}}}\lesssim_\psi \|f\|_{\mathscr FL^q_{v_{s_2}}}$ (valid for $1\le q\le2$ and $p\le1$, or with $s_1$ added for $p>1$), yielding a constant depending on $\Omega$ rather than $|\Omega+\Omega|$.
issues.overall_effect: The local Fourier–Lebesgue and Barron approximation results are unproved as stated; the advertised generalization of Siegel–Xu rests on them.
issues.title: Fourier–Lebesgue/Barron local result: FL^q norm of f does not control the M^{p,q} norm, cutoff not in FL^q_{v_{s_2}}, and s_1 missing for p>1
issues.why_classification: A recognizably comparable result survives (same rate), but it needs a new cutoff argument, a restricted range ($q\ge1$, $p\le1$ or extra $s_1$), and loss of the explicit $|\Omega+\Omega|$ constant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: At this step, in order to obtain a uniform upper bound, it is necessary to assume that the set $\Omega\subset \rrd$ is bounded.

issues.failure_explanation: The STFT inversion formula (eq:f_representation) integrates the spatial variable $y$ over all of $\rr d$, but the dictionary $\bb D_\Omega$ and the measure $\mu_f$ used to place $f$ in $\mathcal K(\tilde{\bb D}_\Omega)$ only contain atoms with $y\in\Omega$. Since $V_\phi f(y,\eta)$ is not supported in $\Omega$ for a general $f\in M^{p,q}_m$ (with a positive Schwartz window it vanishes for all $\eta$ only where $f$ vanishes), the identity $f=\int_{\tilde{\bb D}_\Omega} i\,d\mu_f$ is false, and eq:modulation_space_embedding_in_variation_space is unsupported. Indeed every element of $\mathcal K(\tilde{\bb D}_\Omega)$ is bounded by $\|\mu\|\sup_{y\in\Omega}\langle x\rangle^{s}|\phi(x-y)|$, i.e. decays like the window, whereas $M^{p,q}_{v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2}}$ with $s_1=0$ contains slowly decaying functions. The boundedness of $\Omega$ is exactly what the proof uses to bound $\|v_u\partial^\gamma\phi(\cdot-y)\|_\infty$ uniformly, so the two requirements (full inversion, uniform atom bound) conflict.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must use the full dictionary ($y\in\rr d$) and add a spatial weight $v_u(y)$ ($u$ large enough for the atom bounds) to the dictionary weighting, which forces $f\in M^1_{v_u\otimes v_{n+s}}$ and hence a strictly larger $s_1$ than allowed by eq:indices (in particular $s_1=0$ for $p\le1$ is lost).
issues.overall_effect: The global approximation theorem on $\rr d$, its Feichtinger-algebra and Bessel-potential corollaries, and the introduction's claim about restricted spatial shifts are all unsupported and likely false as stated.
issues.title: Global theorem: representation of f over the restricted dictionary D_Ω is invalid (y is integrated over all of R^d)
issues.why_classification: The central construction fails; any repair changes the dictionary and excludes the advertised weight regime, so no comparable version of the stated theorem survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof integrates $v_{-s}(b)$ over $\rr{}$, which requires $s>1$ strictly, and then needs $f\in M^1_{1\otimes v_{n+s}}$, i.e. $s_2\ge n+s>n+1$ when $q\le1$. The statement, via eq:indices, allows $s_2=n+1$ for $0<q\le1$, which the argument does not cover (the corollary for $p=q=1$ correctly requires $s_2>n+1$). The same endpoint appears in cor:added-3 ($s_2=\lfloor s\rfloor+2$ for $q\le1$). This defect is independent of ISSUE-007.

failure_location.quote: Consider  the weight $m =(v_{s_1}\otimes v_{s_2})$ with $s_1,s_2$ satisfying \eqref{eq:indices}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require $s_2>n+1$ for $q\le1$ in the global theorem and $s_2>\lfloor s\rfloor+2$ in cor:added-3.
issues.overall_effect: The endpoint case $q\le1$, $s_2=n+1$ of the global theorem is unsupported.
issues.title: Global theorem endpoint: s_2 = n+1 for q ≤ 1 is insufficient (proof needs s>1)
issues.why_classification: Replacing an equality by a strict inequality at an endpoint preserves rate, method and scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: then by the identity theorem for analytic functions it would vanish on a non-empty open set

issues.failure_explanation: The triangle inequality gives $|V|\ge|T_2|-|T_1|\le|T_2|$, which cannot imply the claimed strict bound $|V|>\frac1{2\pi}e^{-\pi x^2}$. The bound is in fact false: for $\omega=0$, $x<0$, Theorem relu-stft gives $V(x,0)=\frac{1}{2\pi}e^{-\pi x^2}-\frac{|x|}{2}\operatorname{erfc}(\sqrt\pi|x|)<\frac{1}{2\pi}e^{-\pi x^2}$ (e.g. $x=-1$: $\approx0.0008<0.0069$). The non-vanishing argument is also invalid: a non-constant holomorphic function of two variables can vanish at real points without vanishing on an open set (e.g. $\omega$ itself), so 'never vanishes' is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the strict lower bound and the global non-vanishing claim; state and prove only that $V_\varphi\sigma(t,\tau)\neq0$ for some $\tau\neq0$ (e.g. at $(0,\omega)$), which suffices for Condition (A).
issues.overall_effect: Both assertions of cor:31 are unproved (the lower bound is false). What the paper actually needs, Condition (A) for ReLU with a Gaussian window, still holds (e.g. $\operatorname{Im}V(0,\omega)=-\frac{\omega}{2}e^{-\pi\omega^2}\neq0$ for $\omega\neq0$), so Section 5's use is recoverable.
issues.title: Non-vanishing corollary: false strict lower bound and invalid identity-theorem argument
issues.why_classification: The corollary's own claims must be abandoned or substantially weakened, but the downstream requirement is recovered by a short explicit computation.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate $|\operatorname{erfc}(z)|\le Ce^{-|z|^2}/(1+|z|)$ is false on $\cc{}$: $\operatorname{erfc}(z)\to2$ as $\operatorname{Re}z\to-\infty$ and $|\operatorname{erfc}(iy)|\sim e^{y^2}/(\sqrt\pi y)$ grows. Consequently the claimed bound fails: for $\omega=0$, $V_\varphi\sigma(x,0)=\int_0^\infty te^{-\pi(t-x)^2}dt\sim x$ as $x\to+\infty$, while the right-hand side tends to 0. The same computation shows $\int|V_\varphi\sigma(x,0)|v_s(x)dx=\infty$ for $s\ge-2$, so Remark 33's claim $\sigma\in M^{1,\infty}_{v_s\otimes1}$ for every $s$ is false as well (ReLU is unbounded, in line with the main theorems' hypothesis $\sigma\in W^{k,\infty}$ which ReLU does not satisfy).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must withdraw the Gaussian decay in $x$ and Remark 33, and replace them by a correct growth/decay estimate (polynomial growth in $x$, decay in $\omega$ only for fixed $x$).
issues.overall_effect: cor:relu-decay and rem:33 are false; the claimed time-frequency justification of ReLU within the modulation framework does not hold as stated (the main theorems do not depend on it).
issues.title: Decay estimate for the ReLU STFT is false (erfc bound invalid; STFT grows linearly in x)
issues.why_classification: No comparable version of the stated two-variable Gaussian decay survives; the correct behavior is qualitatively different (linear growth in $x$).
